findings.evidence: smoke_perflab.cpp:7 is `#include "check.h"` and smoke_saveevents.cpp:34 is `#include "FakeKPatchApi.h"`, yet build_check reports `fatal error: check.h: No such file or directory` and `FakeKPatchApi.h: No such file or directory` for all eight harness smoke files (rc 1, FAIL=1). The same `#include "check.h"` at perflab/common_contract_test.cpp:34 compiles and passes in run_tests (rc 0), so the include path is set for one target but not the harness target.
findings.suggested_investigation: Compare the compile flags for the harness target against those used for common_contract_test.cpp (the -I entries for check.h and FakeKPatchApi.h). Confirm whether FakeKPatchApi.h and check.h exist in the snapshot at the paths the build expects. Re-run build_check in a fresh copy that has git history and binaries. Do not record the failure as pre-existing without a written waiver.
findings.why_it_matters: The perf_lab_src build gate fails, so the smoke harnesses (perflab, portraitslots, queuehud, saveevents, selfheal, probes) cannot run. Under the Gate Invariant this is a hard stop and cannot be waved off as a scratch-copy artifact without evidence.

findings.evidence: Heavy post hook: `address = 0x0051D9C1` with `original_bytes = [0x3B, 0x05, 0xB8, 0x44, 0x99, 0x00]` (CMP EAX,[0x9944B8]) and `[[hooks.parameters]] source = "eax"`, bound to `void __cdecl PerfLabAiHeavyPost(int res)` (PerfLab.cpp:1756). Every hook in this block has `exclude_from_restore = []`. The stolen CMP sets the flags that the following Jcc consumes, and the handler is a compiled C++ cdecl function that can clobber EAX/ECX/EDX/EFLAGS.
findings.suggested_investigation: Read the KPM detour trampoline generator to confirm it saves and restores all general-purpose registers and EFLAGS around the cdecl handler call, and that the stolen instruction runs after the handler returns. Check that the parameter `eax` is captured before the handler runs. Then confirm that the same convention holds for the entry hook PerfLabToLower, which reads `ecx`, at 0x734690.
findings.why_it_matters: If the KPM detour trampoline does not save and restore EAX, ECX, EDX and EFLAGS around the handler call, the mid-function hooks at 0x51D9AB, 0x51D9C1 and 0x51D9F1 can change the comparison result or the AI update control flow in normal play. That would be a behaviour change in a perf-only patch.

findings.evidence: The manifest description says the diagnostics are "inert unless perflab_debug.txt exists", but the hooks file installs unconditional detours on hot paths: `address = 0x00734690` (CExoString::ToLower, kotor2-steam-aspyr.hooks.toml:806-812), `address = 0x004999F4` (FocusGob strcmp, lines 797-803), and the texture-id scan entry and exit at 0x427970 and 0x427A51 (lines 779-794). The `g_m`/`g_cfg.metrics` gate is only inside the handlers (PerfLab.cpp:1809-1812, 1803-1805).
findings.suggested_investigation: Check how KPM and the perf-lab init path decide which hooks to install. Confirm whether the 0.6.0 hooks are installed only when perflab_debug.txt exists. If they are installed unconditionally, measure the baseline cost of an idle trampoline on CExoString::ToLower and strcmp.
findings.why_it_matters: If the detours are installed even when the debug file is absent, every ToLower, strcmp and texture scan pays a trampoline cost. That conflicts with the documented inert default, and the measured timings would then include the instrumentation overhead.
